newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Short stg vols climb after retail shock.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Short stg vols climb after retail shock.

text.p: A shocking rise in UK retail sales on Tuesday lifted implied volatility of short sterling options as investors forecast higher interest rates, traders said.

UK retail sales shot up 1.1 percent in May and 5.3 percent in the year, against forecasts of 0.2 percent and 4.5 percent respectively. The three month growth rate was the biggest since the consumer boom of the late 1980s .
The rise heightened fears that building society windfalls are fuelling a spending spree, and could lead to higher interest rates to cool down the overheated economy.
Options traders said the retail data had sparked a buying spree in September short sterling puts, stoking up the volatility to 8.0 percent for the 93.00 strike from around 7.24 on Tuesday.
The rise put to an end the falling trend in vols since the Labour Party's emphatic win in the May election.

"We've seen vols quite aggressively low in the past few weeks. It was probably in sympathy with the Blair honeymoon," said Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures in London. "This may be coming to a close now."
Traders quoted the vol for the December 93.00 strike at around 8.7 percent against 8.33 on Tuesday. The December 92.75 strike was around 9.2 percent.

Wednesday's trades featured a U.S. securities firm buying 2,500 of September 93.00 puts against futures. A UK company took 2,000 September 92.75 puts, apparently taking a punt on the volatility, traders said.
Put straddles also saw strong demand.
Some economists said they were considering reviewing interest rate forecasts in light of the retail data.
But most are likely to wait until the UK Chancellor Gordon Brown delivers his mini-budget on July 2.
A week after that the Bank of England's monetary policy committee will meet on whether to raise interest rates after the May 6 hike of 25 basis points to 6.50 percent.
December interest rate futures are now discounting three month money about 7.13 percent at expiry.

The minutes of the May 6 monetary meeting released on Wednesday hinted that Brown might consider raising personal tax rates instead to remove the inflation threat. They record Brown saying the budget would encourage more "balanced" economic growth.
Some options traders said the vol rise was temporary.
"I think any upward move will be short lived and sold into. Implied vols are historically on the low side and I don't see any reason for an increase," said one.
Activity in gilt options was light and vols were unchanged at 6.6 percent for August and 6.8 percent for September, traders said.
